verses.text: In those days Israel had no king. And in those days the tribe of Dan was looking for a place of their own to settle, because they had not yet received their share of land among the tribes of Israel.

So the people of Dan sent five brave men from their clans, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. They told them, "Go and explore the land." The men came to the hill country of Ephraim and stayed overnight at Micah's house.
When they were near Micah's house, they recognised the voice of the young Levite. So they went over and asked him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?"
He told them what Micah had done for him, and said, "He has hired me, and I am his priest."
Then they said to him, "Please ask God for us whether our journey will be successful."
The priest answered them, "Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey."

So the five men left and came to Laish. They saw that the people there were living in safety, like the Sidonians, peaceful and unsuspecting. They had everything they needed, and no one there was harming them. They lived far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone else.
When the men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, their relatives asked them, "What did you find?"
They answered, "Come on, let us attack them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. Why are you sitting still? Do not wait. Go and take the land.
When you get there, you will find people who suspect nothing, and the land is large. God has given it into your hands, a land that has everything you could want."
So six hundred men of the tribe of Dan, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
On the way they camped near Kiriath Jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath Jearim is still called Mahaneh Dan, which means Camp of Dan.
From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.

Then the five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their relatives, "Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods and a carved idol covered with silver? Now you know what to do."
So they turned in there and went to the house of the young Levite at Micah's place and greeted him.
The six hundred men of Dan, armed for battle, stood at the entrance of the gate.
The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods, while the priest and the six hundred armed men stood at the entrance of the gate.
When the men went into Micah's house and took the idol, the ephod, the household gods and the silver image, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

They answered him, "Be quiet! Do not say a word. Come with us and be our father and priest. Is it not better for you to be priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel than for just one man's household?"
The priest was very pleased. He took the ephod, the household gods and the idol and went along with the people.
They turned and set out again, putting their children, their animals and their belongings in front of them.
When they had gone some distance from Micah's house, the men who lived near Micah were called together and caught up with the people of Dan.
As they shouted after them, the people of Dan turned and said to Micah, "What is wrong with you, that you have called out your men to fight?"
He answered, "You took the gods I made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you ask, 'What is wrong with you?'"
The people of Dan answered, "Do not argue with us, or some angry men may attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives."
So the people of Dan went on their way. Micah saw that they were too strong for him, so he turned around and went home.
Then they took what Micah had made, and his priest, and went on to Laish, against a peaceful people who suspected nothing. They attacked them with swords and burned down their city.

There was no one to rescue them, because they lived far from Sidon and had no dealings with anyone else. The city was in a valley near Beth Rehob. The people of Dan rebuilt the city and settled there.
They named it Dan after their ancestor Dan, who was a son of Israel, though the city used to be called Laish.
There the people of Dan set up the idol for themselves. Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the time the land was taken into captivity.
They kept using the idol Micah had made the whole time the house of God was at Shiloh.
